item.title: Bart Moriarty
item.description: Bart Moriarty, Dunmaniheen, Killorglin and formerly of Killelan, Caherciveen. Died peacefully surrounded by his loving family in University Hospital Kerry on the 13th of January, 2026. Predeceased by his loving wife Nancy, his brother Con, and sister Mary Daly. Sadly missed by his loving daughter Bríd, sons Seán and Tadhg, daughter-in-law Sinéad and beloved grandsons Ben and Dylan, his nephews and nieces, relatives, neighbours and many friends. Rest In Peace Reposing Thursday, 15th January 2026

item.title: Typical diner at Tralee Soup Kitchen changing to reflect economic realities
item.description: The typical diner at Tralee Soup Kitchen is changing. Established in October 2011 in response to the economic crisis, the kitchen was initially expected to be needed for around six months, but has now been operating for 14 years. They provide free three-course meals to between 100 and 120 people from noon and two every Saturday. Advertisement It's a drop-in service with no booking required. item.title: 34 patients waiting on trolleys in University Hospital Kerry
item.description: There are 34 patients waiting on trolleys in University Hospital Kerry today. That’s according to figures provided by the Irish Nurses and Midwives’ Organisation. 24 people are on trolleys in UHK’s emergency department, while a further 10 patients are waiting on trolleys in wards elsewhere within the hospital. Advertisement Nationally, 769 people are waiting for beds in hospitals across the country today.

item.title: Kerry Dairy Ireland drops its December milk price by 3 cent per litre
item.description: Kerry Dairy Ireland has dropped its December milk price by a further 3 cent per litre. It will now pay 34.5 cent per litre including VAT and quality and sustainability bonuses for milk supplied by farmers last month. In its monthly statement, the milk processor says this milk price is equivalent to 37.77 cent per litre including VAT at EU standard constituents (3.4% protein and 4.2% butterfat). item.title: Over €1.7 million in annual premium payments announced for Kerry forest owners
item.description: Over €1.7 million (€1,776,255.92) in annual premium payments has been announced for Kerry forest owners. It’s part of more than €23.5 million in payments nationally, announced by Agriculture Minister Martin Hayden, and Minister of State Michael Healy-Rae. The premiums support forest owners, and grants available under the Afforestation Grant and Premium Scheme cover the cost of establishing forest plantation. item.description: Communications Minister Patrick O’Donovan has criticised the public for not using their local post office This comes after yesterday's Government approval of 75 million euro in funding to support the postal network over the next five years. item.description: An approved housing body is expecting to deliver 100 social homes in Killarney in the coming months. item.title: Plaque to be erected remembering James Lasts’ famous Tralee concerts
item.description: A plaque will be erected in Tralee to pay homage to the famous concerts of James Last in the county capital. The German composer performed shows at Austin Stack Park during the Rose of Tralee Festival in 1983 and 1986. James Last, who passed away in 2015, is reported to have sold an estimated 200 million records worldwide in his lifetime. item.title: HSE cuts home care waiting lists in Kerry by 60% in two and a half years
item.description: The HSE has cut home care waiting lists in Kerry by 60% in the last two and a half years. The latest figures from the Health Service Executive show there are still over 100 people in Kerry awaiting home support. As of the end of November 101 people were awaiting home support in Kerry; just 25 are awaiting new home support service, with 76 awaiting additional hours of home support.
